scope: Five bounded Bun lifecycle tests for the existing native deferred-media release gate; production source unchanged. No Phase 5/6/W26 completion.
setup: One three-byte blob, a named real JournalSession with committed session metadata, real LocalMediaStore, HistoryMediaOwnership bound through its native gate, and JournalProviderRequestSnapshot. The actual decoded pinned historical row resolves through RequestMediaResolver before child self-SIGKILL. Request/owner/media/session orderly cleanup never runs in the killed child. Parent reopens a separate journal descriptor and a new media-store instance.

contracts.crash: Child reclamation removes zero and pinned resolution returns DRUi before self-SIGKILL. Parent sees no inherited pin, durable rel:0/head=0/tail=1, and a still-fresh dead-instance reservation that protects the blob. Owner bind drains through existing owner-digest release semantics without lease expiry; reclamation removes exactly one object and its object path is absent. No artificial clock or sleep is used.
contracts.compaction: Explicit compaction refuses with a live request pin or a nonempty queue after a failed release has closed every pin. Inode, size and mtime are unchanged. Re-adoption before final pin close keeps current media reserved; drain finishes, actual compaction swaps and omits now-empty rel state, and a separate descriptor sees the current row. Clearing it later permits reclamation.
contracts.checkpoints: After drain removes history reservations, actual janitor projectRecordedContentIds protects checkpoint media. Actual compaction and independent owner reopen preserve that protection. Verified access uses a real checkpoint-reader external reservation, then releases it. Checkpoint deletion followed by another actual compaction removes its protected ID and permits reclamation. This does not claim reservation-only protection of retained checkpoints.
contracts.interruptions: A single external-release failure is preserved by identity and leaves head=0 plus rel:0 durable. Independent owner open retries and reclaims. Separately, failure of the state-only head commit after successful external release leaves durable head=0; fresh owner open repeats the already-completed idempotent release through the real store, advances the head and permits reclamation. No error is swallowed by the test or a new wrapper.
contracts.emptyDrain: After drain, settle succeeds while commit and media.release are fault traps. Journal inode/size/mtime and the recursive media-directory inventory are unchanged. No write or release call is accepted.
contracts.boundedness: No production change, deferred-ID RAM collection, per-operation production file, provenance exemption or historical ID scan was introduced. Existing disk FIFO, scalar head/tail, one-entry drain and per-concurrent-version pin bookkeeping are retained. Aggregate pin/cache/janitor/admission capacity is not measured here.

fresh.budget: Each Bun test file runs serially, isolated, with --timeout 180000. No overlapping heavy lane.
fresh.gates: Core declaration emit, existing core noemit project, explicit Bun test-type invocation of that project, actual input-file inventory, scoped ESLint/Prettier, affected-test graph, AST audit and preservation pass. Both new test files appear in the type input list.

broadTypeRed.interpretation: The wider core test project reports diagnostics outside the changed paths. It is not counted as passing and was not repeated or suppressed. No configuration or enforcement was changed. Existing core/tsconfig.noemit.json includes both added files and its Bun test types pass.

controlInterpretation: Ignoring the persisted tail fails actual reclamation (expected 1 object, observed 0), early drain fails protection (expected 0 removals, observed 1), and removing only the pending-release compaction veto loses rel:0 (expected durable entry, observed undefined). The last control retains the live-pin veto and proves why omission of rel entries in the compaction copy needs the pending-queue veto. These are assertion failures, not syntax/runtime-only controls. Every original is restored with cmp and SHA256. The restoration-omission control ignores the persisted tail; it does not claim to mutate entry serialization itself.
reused: No historical memory or lifetime measurement is promoted. Prior declarations-after inventory is reused only as the comparison baseline; every current declaration is freshly hashed. Corpus, reader and gate test results above are fresh. Early three-test commit used abrupt exit 77; final-source crash proof uses SIGKILL and adds checkpoint/head-write cases. Initial fixture output-capture/setup and lint failures remain in initial-receipts, not counted as contract REDs.

audit.interpretation: One DUP_ASSERT checks zero reclamation at two distinct lifecycle points: deferred old pin, then re-adopted live current owner after compaction. Both assertions remain enabled. No changed-file MOCK_MIRROR, ALWAYS_TRUE, SELF_CONFIRMING or NO_ASSERT finding remains. Initial readFile temporal-equality warnings were replaced by explicit unchanged inode/size/mtime assertions, with independent lost-entry mutation proof.

preservation.note: Raw recovery, dirty memory and all inherited declarations remain untouched and unstaged. Fixture renamed to the existing test-helper convention so declaration builds do not treat it as production.

open: Original full native 1/8 MiB text/tool memory protocols remain pending for prior production changes; no new memory acceptance is claimed.
Aggregate cache/pin/overlay/admission-owner/janitor capacity, tombstone/live-byte and global LENS accounting remain pending.

Crash between history removal and durable queue append; torn queue commit; forced automatic-compaction-on-owner-open ordering; deterministic stale-instance expiry; process-kill during an actual external release and between release and head ack remain untested. The new interrupted-head case uses the existing commit fault seam, not an OS power-loss claim.
A retained checkpoint plus compaction/reopen is proved; fork/restore adoption across process crash is not independently covered. Re-adoption here is before old-pin drain in one live owner.

Actual HTTP semantic-purge/abort combinations, independent post-registration adoption/raw synchronous-add proof, last-thinking/pruned views, other providers and native log/dump remain outside this proof.
prohibited: No production redesign, enforcement changes, cleanup, .llxprt edits/staging, OCR, default flip, push or merge.
